extracted.intended_audience: NSF program officers, principal investigators, university/college research administrators, and NSF oversight officials
extracted.subtask_description: Policies, procedures, and evaluative criteria governing the National Science Foundation's peer review of grant proposals, reconsideration procedures, and oversight/monitoring of program review processes. Includes guidance on reviewer selection, openness, confidentiality, and institutional fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair and impartial evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals should be evaluated to result in funding of the highest quality science and applicants whose proposal has been declined shall have an opportunity to receive an explanation and reconsideration where the applicant has reason to believe the proposal did not receive a fair and impartial initial evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reconsideration is not adversary; Program Director must explain basis for declination; Assistant Director and Deputy Director have specified review roles to determine fairness; administrative judgments and peer review adequacy may be reexamined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad participation of qualified reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Program officers should seek broadly representative participation of qualified individuals as reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board instructed program officers to seek panel and advisory group members from all types of institutions, including colleges; lists of suitable college faculty have been prepared and provided to NSF program officers to increase representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness and information to proposers consistent with effective evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: The review process should be conducted as openly as possible and with as much information to proposers as possible, consistent with the effective evaluation of proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes offering verbatim review copies (with identities redacted as specified), informing PIs of reasons for decisions, and publishing reviewer lists annually (subject to confidentiality rules and historical commitments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of reviewers list
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation will publish annually a list of all reviewers used by each Division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is intended to increase transparency and understanding of the review process; the Board also recommended studying whether less aggregated publication might be desirable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of verbatim reviews to proposers (with identity redaction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Verbatim copies of reviews requested by the Foundation after January 1, 1976, not including the identity of the reviewer, will be made available to the principal investigator/project director upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews solicited prior to January 1, 1976 remain governed by earlier confidentiality commitments; the Board will consider whether to include reviewer identity later and urged caution in changing confidentiality levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informing PIs of reasons for decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation, upon request, will inform the principal investigator/project director of the reasons for its decision on the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program Directors should furnish information concerning the basis for NSF action including verbatim comments of peer reviews (with identifying data deleted as required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of reviewers from all types of institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase Foundation use of college faculty members as ad hoc proposal reviewers and advisory panel members to increase perception of fairness among college faculties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSB encouraged use of suitable persons from colleges and noted existing lists (e.g., AASCU list of over 700 faculty) to assist program officers; reasonable expectation remains that many reviewers will be active researchers at universities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of institutional constraints in evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers and decision-makers should recognize and make allowance for the effect of teaching loads and the necessity to supervise less-experienced research assistants, both of which restrict research output from scientists in colleges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This recognition is intended to reduce bias against applicants at teaching-focused institutions when judging quantity or productivity measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of equipment and facility limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Continue to develop arrangements enabling scientists at institutions with equipment limitations to work at well-equipped laboratories part-time or during summers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where field/discipline requires specialized facilities, the concentration of awards may be explained; procedures should allow equitable access despite local equipment constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to requirement for external peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of all formal proposals for NSF funding includes external peer review with specified exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions include: proposals governed by Federal Procurement Regulations, proposals to provide goods/services normally purchased, proposals for which peer review has been waived by the Director (with reporting), and proposals withdrawn prior to decision. Some classes (travel grants, committed renewals) may be categorically excepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary method of peer review for each program
rubrics_metrics.description: Each program shall select one primary method for peer review which will represent the minimum review received by proposals in that program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary methods include ad hoc/mail reviews, assembled panel reviews, or combinations; primary method can be supplemented with additional reviews, site visits, etc.; after Director approval the primary method and evaluation criteria shall be announced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection and performance quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection and performance of reviewers should be judged excellent and is a metric in program oversight reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External program reviews will examine selection and performance of reviewers as part of assessing program quality; example chemistry review found reviewer selection/performance excellent even when budgets were tight.

rubrics_metrics.name: External program oversight review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: External reviews of Foundation programs should examine scientific quality and balance, decisionmaking procedures, funding decisions, and quality of program management, including the adequacy of peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review teams will have complete access to information, will monitor adequacy of decisionmaking under proposal pressure, and may recommend procedural improvements; detailed procedures are being developed (trial in chemistry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring metrics for program health
rubrics_metrics.description: Program oversight should consider metrics such as average grant size, adequacy of subprogram budgets, correlation between proposal quality and funds allocated, and overall funding of best proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the chemistry trial: average grant size too small in all cases; some subprogram budgets much too small; one 'failure of correlation' noted; yet decisionmaking quality was maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration — explanation by Program Director
rubrics_metrics.description: A Principal Investigator desiring information concerning a declination should request an explanation from the appropriate Program Director, who will furnish information concerning the basis for NSF action and offer opportunity to present PI's point of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program Director will provide verbatim comments of reviews (with identifying data deleted for reviews solicited after Jan 1, 1976); changes to proposals after declination are not considered in reconsideration but may be submitted as new proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration — request to Assistant Director (first-level)
rubrics_metrics.description: PI may request in writing that the Foundation reconsider its action provided request follows the Program Director's explanation and is postmarked/received within 180 days of the declination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request directed to Assistant Director of the relevant Directorate, must set forth facts why reconsideration is warranted; Assistant Director must not be someone who participated in initial evaluation; may obtain additional peer review; must respond in writing within 60 days (or notify of delay).

rubrics_metrics.name: Further reconsideration — Deputy Director (second-level)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 180 days following the Assistant Director reconsideration, the institution (or individual where no institution) may request further reconsideration by the Deputy Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request must be in writing, signed by Authorized Institutional Representative and PI(s), state proposal ID/title, set forth reasons and supporting facts; Deputy Director (or designee not involved previously) will reexamine administrative judgments and obtain additional peer review if inadequate or unfair peer review influenced judgments; written report within 30 days (or notify of delay). Finality: once Deputy Director reconsideration complete, no further reconsideration of that proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of reconsideration reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Reconsideration examines whether the proposal received fair consideration and reexamines administrative judgments; if evidence shows administrative judgments were influenced by inadequate or unfair peer review, additional peer review will be obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Officials conducting reconsideration may request more information from PI and may obtain further peer review comments; outcomes include affirmation of declination or notification of availability of further review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution in changing confidentiality levels
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board recommended collecting further information concerning effects on peer review of the level of confidentiality in which reviewers' names and verbatim comments are held; changes in confidentiality should be made slowly if at all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reflects balance between openness and effective evaluation; reviews solicited before Jan 1, 1976 remain under earlier confidentiality commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable access and non-discrimination among institution types
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board recognizes responsibility to ensure available research monies are equally accessible to all performers and that scientists in 4-year colleges are not discriminated against.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions to achieve this include increasing college faculty reviewers, recognizing teaching/equipment constraints, enabling access to well-equipped labs, and continuing Board oversight to minimize biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board responsibility for peer review policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Science Board should have primary responsibility for the establishment of policies governing peer review at the National Science Foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcommittee recommended the Board study topics (support for innovative research, young scientists, college funding, extent of reliance on peer panels), establish internal monitoring programs, and report periodically to Congress on mismatch and peer review procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program planning environment review
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual review of disciplines assessing infrastructure, manpower, funding, and political factors affecting research capabilities, to identify significant policy issues for Board decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The planning environment review is used to identify areas requiring further study or action and to provide basis for budgetary recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multiple review mechanisms as needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary peer review method may be supplemented with additional reviews, site visits, and other procedures on a per-proposal basis to ensure adequate evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs must announce their primary review method and criteria after Director approval; additional mechanisms may be used to address special cases or unusual proposal needs.
